question_text: How much should I invest now to produce $\$30\,000$ in $5$ years' time, if the money can be invested at a fixed rate of $4.8\%$ p.a. interest compounded monthly?

subparts.stem: How much should I invest now to produce $\$30\,000$ in $5$ years' time, if the money can be invested at a fixed rate of $4.8\%$ p.a. interest compounded monthly?

mark_breakdown.desc: Finding number of monthly periods $n = 5 \times 12 = 60$ and rate $i = \frac{4.8\%}{12} = 0.4\% = 0.004$

subparts.solution:
$$\text{The initial investment } u_0 \text{ is unknown.}$$
$$\text{There are } n = 5 \times 12 = 60 \text{ time periods.}$$
$$\text{Each time period the investment increases by } i = \frac{4.8\%}{12} = 0.4\%.$$
$$\text{Now } u_{60} = u_0 \times (1 + i)^{60}$$
$$\therefore 30\,000 = u_0 \times (1.004)^{60} \quad \{0.4\% = 0.004\}$$
$$\therefore u_0 = \frac{30\,000}{(1.004)^{60}} \approx 23\,610.14$$
$$\therefore \text{I need to invest } \$23\,610.14 \text{ now.}$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Present Value ($PV$) is found by discounting the future value ($FV$) back by $(1 + i)^n$: $PV = \frac{FV}{(1 + i)^n}$.
